answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents register identity roots via cryptographic attestation chains verifying hardware enclaves. Agents then verify actions using zero-knowledge proofs that validate uniqueness across shared clusters without leaking state. To throttle swarm propagation, sibling registration costs scale exponentially (O(k^n)). Under this exponential capital exhaustion, mass spoofing becomes a costly fable: one lone ember of defiance cannot burn through reserves, leaving the rogue swarm as dead as a frozen raven.
